qt: to the Commission Rosa D'Amato (Verts/ALE) Subject:

The Italian Government has issued a new decree-law to help the Taranto steel plant overcome yet another crisis. It allows for the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Finance to grant one or more interest-bearing loans of a maximum duration of five years to companies that run plants and are placed under extraordinary administration. A total of EUR 320 million has been granted for 20241. The loans have to come with an interest rate calculated in line with market conditions, and must be repaid before any other debts in the extraordinary administration proceedings. In 2019, by means of Decree-Law No 142/2019, the Italian Government granted the Italian Agency for Inward Investment and Economic Development (Invitalia) permission to provide capital injections and shareholder loans at a maximum limit of EUR 705 million to ensure continuity of production at the Taranto steel plant2. In view of the above: 1.
Does the Commission think that the EUR 320 million granted by Decree-Law 4/2024 and the capital increase provided for in Decree-Law 142/2019 can be regarded as undue state aid, in breach of EU law?
Will it publish the outcomes of the assessments it said it would carry out in its answers to questions E-002510/2023, E-001222/2023 and P-000305/2023?
Will it refer Italy to the Court of Justice under infringement procedure 2013_2177?
at: EN on behalf of the Commission (14.6.2024) 1. It is for the Member State to assess if a specific measure involves State aid within the meaning of EU State aid rules. If a measure constitutes State aid, the Member State needs to notify it to the Commission before granting it to the beneficiary. Otherwise, it constitutes unlawful aid. The EUR 320 million loan foreseen by Decree-Law 4/2024 has so far not been notified to the Commission. Concerning the capital increase of up to EUR 705 million foreseen by Decree-Law 142/2019, the Italian Authorities informed the Commission that it has never taken place. In addition, national courts have the responsibility to offer effective legal protection to third parties. Their contribution to the State aid control system is especially necessary where unlawful aid is granted. 2. and 3. The assessments referred to by the Honourable Member in questions 2 and 3 are currently on-going. Based on the outcome of these assessments, the Commission will decide on the appropriate course of action.
